result: Pathway R-HSA-209968, Thyroxine biosynthesis (review status five stars, externally reviewed), and its reactions, read through the Reactome Content Service on 2026-10-21. SLC5A5 (NIS) transports iodide from blood serum into thyroid cells using the inward movement of Na+, which the Na+/K+-ATPase drives; TSH stimulates the uptake; SLC5A5 mutations cause thyroid dyshormonogenesis 1. DUOX1 and DUOX2 form the H2O2 that thyroid peroxidase requires. TPO, with cofactors Ca2+ and haem b, in a complex on the extracellular side of the apical plasma membrane, iodinates tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin with iodide and H2O2 and transfers the iodophenyl group of a donor DIT to an acceptor DIT (T4) or MIT (T3), leaving dehydroalanine on the donor; TPO mutations cause thyroid dyshormonogenesis 2A. Iodinated thyroglobulin is taken into follicular cells and cleaved in lysosomes, releasing T4, T3 and iodotyrosines; released iodide is recycled, and T4 and T3 are exported to the blood. DIO3 converts T4 to reverse T3 and T3 to 3,3'-diiodothyronine (T2), both inactive.
